findings.finding: Final current-access check preceded a potentially blocking workspace advisory lock.
findings.correction: preparedAccess now obtains ws:<canonical workspace id> inside its outer atomic transaction before assertWorkspaceAccess, then checks request cancellation after the wait. recordAccess reuses the transaction-owned lock, removing the later lock wait after authorization.
findings.coverage: Auth semantics, role floors and identity attribution unchanged. No network is performed under this SQL lock. Applies to prepared auditor views, ZIP and legacy exports, access reads and file downloads.
findings.regressions: SQLite-safe cancellation during final lock wait passes. Two PostgreSQL-only cases hold an actual workspace advisory lock after blob preparation, observe an ungranted lock in pg_locks, commit membership/token revocation, then release the lock and require denial without bytes or an access record.

findings.finding: A same-workspace live summary refresh hid a disabled framework without removing its selected id.
findings.correction: Requests and enabled buttons use selection intersected with current framework availability. An availability-key layout effect preserves valid user selections, removes invalid ids, aborts active work, and clears capture, receipt, error and loading state before painting the new scope. Late aborted results cannot restore removed-scope data. Newly enabled frameworks remain user-selectable rather than silently widening a prior selection.
findings.regressions: Authored a browser journey that opens a preview and saves a receipt, holds a second response, disables one framework through another signed-in owner request, waits for the real live summary refresh, releases the stale response, and verifies preview/download recover with only the still-selected valid framework. Authored only; not browser-executed.
